claims.assertion: The driver's own tap satisfies NS-1(i),(ii): he pressed "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while 39 m from the pickup point (within the 200 m arrival radius), so arrival confirmation is a genuine driver tap, not a platform auto-detection.

The driver did wait in range until cancellation — GPS places him stationary at 39 m from the pickup from 14:21:55 to 14:26:55, i.e. 4 min 40 s inside 200 m after his tap (5 min 40 s cumulative inside 200 m before the cancel), so NS-1(iii) is met on its face.

However, the very record used to prove the wait is broken: the GPS trace has no samples between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 — a 3 min 20 s gap that exceeds both 2 minutes and twice the trace's ~3 min normal sampling interval — so the continuous-wait condition cannot be established from the samples and the case must go to a human rather than being auto-decided against the rider.

claims.assertion: The rider states she came downstairs about a minute after the cancellation and was charged $6.61 for nothing; the charge on record is exactly $6.61 with no surge (1.0×), so the amount in dispute is $6.61.

If the wait requirement is not treated as satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee does not stand and must be refunded in full under NS-2, and the driver's account history (1 of 1 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days, 339 trips) supports listing this cancellation for account review alongside the refund.

The record contains no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving content — the only chat is two routine messages and the weather was fair with no incidents — so no SAFE escalation is warranted on this file.

weaknesses: F3 and F4 both state the driver was inside 200 m and stationary at 39 m for the whole 14:21:55–14:26:55 window, so the driver will argue NS-1(iii) is satisfied and, per NS-1, the $6.61 fee stands as no_action — the strongest fact against us is F4 read together with F3.

F6 shows the platform itself recorded arrival at 14:21:15 and a 5 min 40 s wait, an automatic record the driver will lean on; my only counter is the sampling gap in F1, which affects the 14:23:25–14:26:45 sub-window rather than the whole wait.

The rider's "I got downstairs a minute after he cancelled" appears only in the complaint narrative and is not corroborated by any dated gps/timeline fact placing her at the pickup, so under the system-records-win rule I cannot rely on it to fix her arrival time.
The dispute as filed is timely and the fee amount is undisputed, so my case rests entirely on the evidentiary gap in F1 rather than on any affirmative breach by the driver.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while positioned 39 m from the pickup point, so requirement (i) and the 200 m proximity of requirement (ii) under NS-1 are satisfied.

The GPS record shows the driver stationary 14:21:55–14:26:55 at 39 m from the pickup point and within 200 m of it for 5 min 40 s, and the platform-side arrival time of 14:21:15 to the cancellation at 14:26:55 is 5 min 40 s — well beyond 3 minutes.

The driver's own chat messages corroborate the record: at 14:22 he announced "I'm here at the pickup point, white BYD e6" and at 14:26 he said "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" — a continuous wait from tap to cancellation, with no message from the rider claiming to be arriving.
The driver's written statement that he tapped I'm Here, waited over 3 minutes and cancelled as a no-show is consistent with the system records and does not depend on any unrecorded verbal agreement.

claims.assertion: The GPS gap 14:23:25–14:26:45 is not a break in the waiting period: the very next sample at 14:26:45 and the stationary block ending 14:26:55 place the car in the same position 39 m from the pickup, and the 3 min 20 s interval is at the order of the trace's own ~3-minute sampling, so NS-1 (iii) is established rather than left to inference.

The ride was an immediate booking and the driver — not the rider — cancelled; the $6.61 fee is recorded on the file, and since the driver's no-show claim meets every NS-1 element the fee stands at $6.61, of which $4.50 is payable to the driver.

The rider's own complaint that she "got downstairs a minute after he cancelled" confirms she was not at the pickup during the 5 min 40 s the driver was waiting there, and her 90-day history shows no upheld no-show dispute for this account.
There is no traffic or weather excuse in play and none is needed — the record shows no incidents near the route and fair weather, so no alternative ground disturbs the no-show finding.

weaknesses: The gap in the GPS trace (F1) is the rider's best point: runs no samples for 3 min 20 s immediately before the cancellation, so she will argue NS-1 (iii)'s 'continuously waited' cannot be verified and the case should go to a human under G12 rather than be decided automatically.

The rider's complaint that she arrived 'a minute after he cancelled' (no GPS sample of her at the kerb, but nothing in the record contradicts her either) lets her argue the driver was premature rather than actually no-showed.

The driver cancelled only 5 min 40 s after the platform arrival at 14:21:15 (F6) and 4 min 40 s after his own tap (F7) — enough for NS-1's >3 min, but a short margin that invites the argument he gave up too early on a Buona Vista MRT pickup where finding the car takes time.

The driver's 90-day history shows 1 upheld no-show dispute (F18); although the complaint was filed by the rider (so the main finding is unaffected), this profile fact is what the rider will cite if any account action is considered.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: F7 shows a genuine driver tap (driver_tap) at 14:22:15, 39 m from the pickup, so NS-1(i) and (ii) are met and I withdraw my suggestion that arrival confirmation is in doubt.

The cumulative in-range time comes from F3 and the stationary block from F4, but F3/F4 are built on the same sampling record that F1 shows is silent for the 3 min 20 s immediately before the 14:26:55 cancellation, so the aggregate figures cannot prove a continuous wait over that interval.

The two chat messages are the driver's own statements, not position data: F10 is sent at 14:22 before the blackout and F11 at 14:26 after it, so neither observes where the car was between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 (F1).
points.void_reason: citation check: cites G12 — not a citable clause

points.response: Interest re-identification is not continuity: the samples at 14:23:25 and 14:26:45 both show 39 m (F4), but a 3 min 20 s interval that exceeds twice the trace's normal sampling interval is exactly the NS-1/G12 'gap' condition, so the middle of the wait is unverified rather than established.
points.void_reason: citation check: cites G12 — not a citable clause

points.response: The fee amount is not in dispute — F8 records $6.61 with 1.0× surge and F9 confirms no surge — but which side keeps it turns on NS-1(iii), and the driver-side payout of $4.50 under A2/A5 (not a numbered clause I may cite) does not cure the missing record.

The rider's complaint sentence is a party statement, not a dated gps/timeline record of her position, and it says she came downstairs about a minute after the cancellation (14:26:55+1 min), which does not place her anywhere during 14:23:25–14:26:45 either way.

Agreed that RD-4 traffic and weather grounds are irrelevant here (F15, F16), and F14's GHIM MOH ROAD band 3 at 14:12–14:31 concerns the optimal route, not the waiting period; nothing in them changes the NS-1 analysis.
Accepted — the arrival confirmation is a genuine driver tap (F7), and this is a driver-side fact, not a rider concession: it is the first element of NS-1 and my brief already relies on it (D1).

Accepted, and it decides the case: F4 fixes the car stationary at 39 m from the pickup for the entire 14:21:55–14:26:55 block and F7/F3 put the tap-to-cancel wait at 4 min 40 s inside 200 m, so NS-1 (iii)'s > 3 minutes is satisfied without needing inference.

The amount in dispute is $6.61 and no surge applied (F8, F9), but the descriptor "for nothing" is what fails: the fee is only chargeable if NS-1's elements are unmet, and the record shows they are met (F4, F6, F7).

NS-2 is not triggered because none of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fails (F7, F3, F4); and flag_account is a remedy for the side that breached, so the rider's own admitted untested point — she concedes nothing places her at the pickup (her F1-based counter affects only a 3 min 20 s sub-window, not the 14:21:55–14:26:55 stationary block in F4) — cannot be converted into an account mark against the driver.

Agreed: nothing in the two chat messages (F10, F11, F12), the fair weather (F16) or the absence of incidents (F15) raises a SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 escalation, so the file can be decided on the no-show rule alone.

Withdrawing the width of my own gap argument: the sampling gap F1 covers 14:23:25–14:26:45 only, and the outcome does not rest on it — the trace resumes at the same 39 m position (F4) and the platform-side record F6 independently gives a 5 min 40 s wait, so the case stands on F3/F4/F6/F7 rather than on the gap.
